behavior_items: The reproducer is a C++20 modules test that defines a named module `M` and places an `inline` function inside the module interface. Even though the bug report text shows a global module fragment plus `#include <source_location>` followed by `export module M;`, the essential exercised pattern is the same: module compilation is active, and the compiler must serialize module-owned declarations and expressions for later import/use.

The function body calls `std::source_location::current()`, which is not an ordinary library function from the compiler's point of view. GCC treats it as a builtin-like facility and folds it during semantic processing so it can materialize source-location data corresponding to the call site. That means compilation does more than type-check a normal call: it synthesizes internal tree nodes representing the backing storage and the returned `std::source_location` object.

Because `foo` is `inline`, its definition must be preserved in a form suitable for cross-translation-unit use. Under modules, that means GCC's module machinery has to stream the function body and all referenced trees into the BMI / module representation. Inline definitions are therefore a strong trigger for serialization bugs: hidden implementation trees that would otherwise stay local now need to be exported or at least faithfully encoded.

The failure happens during module streaming, not during parsing of the `module` or `export module` line itself. The diagnostic is anchored at the module declaration because that is when GCC is finalizing or writing module state, but the backtrace shows the real activity is in `cp/module.cc` routines such as `tree_value`, `tree_node_vals`, `core_vals`, and `tree_node`, which walk and serialize internal C++ trees.

The root cause described in the report is that `fold_builtin_source_location` creates an implicit `VAR_DECL` to back the `std::source_location::current()` result, but this synthesized declaration has no `DECL_CONTEXT`. In GCC's internal representation, `DECL_CONTEXT` tells the compiler what enclosing scope or owner a declaration belongs to, and the modules implementation expects that relationship to exist when serializing declarations.

When the module streamer encounters that context-less `VAR_DECL`, it reaches an assertion/check in `cp/module.cc` around `tree_node` because it cannot encode the declaration as a well-formed module entity. In other words, the compiler is not rejecting user code for semantic reasons; it is crashing because an internal node produced by a builtin transformation violates module serialization invariants.

The reproducer specifically exercises the interaction of three subsystems: C++20 modules, inline function body preservation, and builtin folding for source-location capture. Each subsystem works in isolation often enough, but the combination exposes that the synthesized source-location backing declaration was never prepared for module streaming.

`std::source_location::current()` is special because it is call-site-sensitive. The returned object conceptually embeds filename, line, column, and function-name information from the place where `current()` appears. Implementations commonly realize this with hidden static or compiler-generated objects. GCC's folding path therefore invents declarations that do not appear in user code, and those hidden declarations become part of the inline function's serialized body under modules.

The bug report notes that if the immediate assertion about missing `DECL_CONTEXT` is bypassed, additional module-specific problems appear. In particular, the backing declaration name is generated using a global `source_location_id` counter. A single global counter is fragile for modules because separately compiled module units or imported entities can create identically named synthesized declarations or otherwise observe inconsistent numbering, leading to clashes or incorrect merging.

That secondary issue matters because module compilation requires stable identity and reproducible ownership for synthesized entities across compilation boundaries. A naming scheme based only on process-global incrementing state is insufficient when declarations may be emitted into different BMIs, imported later, or instantiated in multiple contexts.

The alternative testcase in the report demonstrates the semantic risk beyond the ICE: an inline function in a header unit or imported header returns `std::source_location::current()`, and another call to `current()` happens in the importing TU. The test compares file-name characters from the two results. This checks whether GCC preserves distinct call-site information correctly across module/import boundaries instead of accidentally reusing or colliding hidden backing objects.

Semantically, the inline helper `foo()` should report the file location of the `current()` expression inside the header or module where `foo` is defined, while the direct call in `main()` should report the location inside `main.cpp`. If module streaming mis-associates the hidden source-location backing declaration, the two objects might alias incorrectly, carry the wrong provenance, or be emitted with conflicting internal names.

The ICE therefore indicates more than a missing null check: it reveals that GCC's modules serializer assumes every declaration reachable from an exported/inline entity has complete contextual ownership metadata, but the source-location builtin path violates that assumption by synthesizing a declaration that behaves like a real declaration without giving it a real enclosing context.

The command line `g++ -fmodules -std=c++20 -S test.cpp` is enough to trigger the problem because assembly generation requires full front-end semantic completion and module emission, but no linking or runtime execution is involved. This is a pure compile-time front-end failure.

From a compiler-behavior perspective, the reproducer confirms that GCC recognizes `std::source_location::current()` early enough to fold it before module output, and that the crash occurs while traversing the resulting trees for serialization. The repeated stack frames in `tree_node`/`tree_value`/`core_vals` suggest recursive streaming through a nested tree structure until it reaches the malformed declaration and aborts.

In short, the reproducer exercises GCC's handling of compiler-generated, call-site-sensitive declarations inside an inline function that must be module-streamed. The internal compiler error occurs because the hidden `VAR_DECL` created for `std::source_location::current()` lacks the `DECL_CONTEXT` metadata required by the modules implementation, and even after that is addressed, unique naming and emission of those hidden declarations across modules remain correctness concerns.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: The reproducer is not testing ordinary user-visible semantics of `std::source_location` alone; it specifically stresses GCC's module serialization of an inline function whose body contains a call-site-sensitive builtin expansion. GCC folds `std::source_location::current()` by creating an implicit backing `VAR_DECL`, but that internal declaration is left without a `DECL_CONTEXT`. When the C++20 modules machinery later streams the inline function body into module state, it assumes every reachable declaration has valid ownership/context information and crashes in `cp/module.cc` when serializing the malformed node. The bug report further shows that fixing the immediate ICE is not sufficient by itself, because the generated backing declarations also rely on a global ID-based naming scheme that is unsafe across module boundaries and can cause collisions or wrong source-location identity after import.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The common pattern is the interaction of three GCC front-end mechanisms: C++20 module serialization, preservation of an inline function body for export/import, and special folding of `std::source_location::current()` into compiler-generated trees. This is not a normal library call path; `fold_builtin_source_location` synthesizes hidden declarations and values that become reachable from the inline function body. The ICE occurs when `cp/module.cc` serializes those trees into module state and encounters an internal declaration that violates module-streaming invariants. The bug report explicitly states that the implicit backing `VAR_DECL` has no `DECL_CONTEXT`, so the modules streamer cannot determine valid ownership/scope for that declaration. A second recurring pattern is unstable identity for synthesized source-location backing objects: naming them from a global `source_location_id` counter is not module-safe, because imported/header-unit/module contexts require reproducible, collision-free identities across separately emitted BMIs and importing translation units. Together, the failure pattern points to defects in how GCC creates, contextualizes, names, and emits compiler-generated source-location declarations when those declarations become part of serialized inline/module entities.
possible_causes: `fold_builtin_source_location` creates an implicit backing `VAR_DECL` without initializing `DECL_CONTEXT`, leaving a malformed declaration that `cp/module.cc` cannot serialize for module export/import.

The C++ modules serializer in `cp/module.cc` assumes every reachable declaration from an inline/module-owned body has valid ownership metadata, but the builtin source-location expansion path violates that invariant and is not normalized before streaming.

Compiler-generated declarations for `std::source_location::current()` are assigned identities/names using a process-global `source_location_id` counter, which is not stable or unique across modules, header units, or imported BMIs, causing clashes or incorrect merging.

Emission logic for hidden source-location backing objects is incomplete for module contexts: the compiler may fail to attach them to the right enclosing function/module scope or to mark them for correct serialization and later re-materialization.

Cross-module handling of call-site-sensitive builtin expansions is incorrect: GCC may treat the synthesized source-location object as an ordinary local implementation detail even when it must be preserved as part of an exported inline definition.

There may be a broader bug in module streaming of compiler-generated tree nodes reachable from folded builtins, where special-case nodes created outside normal declaration-building paths bypass the context/ownership setup that ordinary declarations receive.
evidence: The ICE stack is entirely in C++ module streaming code (`cp/module.cc`: `tree_node`, `core_vals`, `tree_node_vals`, `tree_value`), showing the crash happens during serialization rather than parsing or ordinary semantic analysis.

The report directly identifies the immediate cause: the implicit `VAR_DECL` created in `fold_builtin_source_location` has no `DECL_CONTEXT`, and modules rely on that field to stream declarations correctly.
The reproducer requires an `inline` function inside a module interface, which forces GCC to preserve and serialize the function body and every hidden tree referenced from it.

`std::source_location::current()` is call-site-sensitive and implemented through compiler folding/synthesized backing storage, so hidden internal declarations are expected to appear in the serialized tree graph.

The bug report says that disabling the assertion reveals further issues with the global `source_location_id` naming scheme, indicating the problem is not only a missing null/context check but also incorrect identity management across modules.

The alternative testcase involving an imported header and a direct call in `main` demonstrates the expected need for distinct, correctly attributed source-location objects across module/import boundaries, which would be broken by collisions or wrong ownership of the synthesized declarations.

selected_files.reason: The ICE stack is entirely in this file (`tree_node`, `tree_value`, `tree_node_vals`, `core_vals`), and the report explicitly says the modules streamer relies on `DECL_CONTEXT` and crashes when serializing the malformed implicit `VAR_DECL`.

`std::source_location::current()` is folded in the C++ front end, and the reported root cause names `fold_builtin_source_location` as creating the implicit backing `VAR_DECL` without a proper `DECL_CONTEXT`; this file is a strong candidate for that folding/semantic expansion logic.

The bug involves synthesizing hidden C++ trees for `std::source_location` inside an inline function, and this file contains core C++ tree-building helpers such as `build_target_expr`; it is a plausible place where the generated declaration/object is constructed without full ownership metadata.

The failure is specifically about a synthesized `VAR_DECL` lacking declaration context, and this file owns much of C++ declaration construction and context attachment, making it a likely place where an implicit declaration should be initialized or normalized for modules.

If the malformed node is created with incomplete low-level tree state, the underlying tree allocation/initialization code here could be involved, especially around default declaration fields later assumed by module streaming.

Although the immediate crash is in C++ module-specific streaming rather than generic LTO streaming, the bug is fundamentally about serializing a compiler-generated tree node, so generic tree streaming support is a secondary suspect for assumptions about declaration completeness.

The broader issue is streaming internal tree graphs with hidden declarations, and this shared streamer infrastructure may encode invariants that the source-location-generated `VAR_DECL` violates when reached through module serialization.

The secondary correctness issue concerns `std::source_location` provenance such as file names and call-site identity; while not the most likely ICE source, this file participates in source file/name handling used by source-location materialization.

gcc/cp/semantics.cc.summary: Helper function for handle_omp_array_sections. Called recursively to handle multiple array-section-subscripts. C is the clause, T current expression (initially OMP_CLAUSE_DECL), which is either a TREE_LIST for array-section-subscript (TREE_PURPOSE is low-bound expression if specified, TREE_VALUE length expression if specified, TREE_CHAIN is what it has been specified after, or some decl. TYPES vector is populated with array section types, MAYBE_ZERO_LEN set to true if any of the array-section-subscript could have length of zero (explicit or implicit), FIRST_NON_ONE is the index of the first array-section-subscript which is known not to have length of one. Given say: map(a[:b][2:1][:c][:2][:d][e:f][2:5]) FIRST_NON_ONE will be 3, array-section-subscript [:b], [2:1] and [:c] all are or may have length of 1, array-section-subscript [:2] is the first one known not to have length 1. For array-section-subscript <= FIRST_NON_ONE we diagnose non-contiguous arrays if low bound isn't 0 or length isn't the array domain max + 1, for > FIRST_NON_ONE we can if MAYBE_ZERO_LEN is false. gcc/cp/tree.cc.summary: Make a variant of TYPE, qualified with the TYPE_QUALS. Handles arrays correctly. In particular, if TYPE is an array of T's, and TYPE_QUALS is non-empty, returns an array of qualified T's. FLAGS determines how to deal with ill-formed qualifications. If tf_ignore_bad_quals is set, then bad qualifications are dropped (this is permitted if TYPE was introduced via a typedef or template type parameter). If bad qualifications are dropped and tf_warning is set, then a warning is issued for non-const qualifications. If tf_ignore_bad_quals is not set and tf_error is not set, we return error_mark_node. Otherwise, we issue an error, and ignore the qualifications. Qualification of a reference type is valid when the reference came via a typedef or template type argument. [dcl.ref] No such dispensation is provided for qualifying a function type. [dcl.fct] DR 295 queries this and the proposed resolution brings it into line with qualifying a reference. We implement the DR. We also behave in a similar manner for restricting non-pointer types.

gcc/cp/tree.cc.signature: tree strip_typedefs (tree t, bool *remove_attributes , unsigned int flags )
gcc/cp/tree.cc.summary: Builds a qualified variant of T that is either not a typedef variant (the default behavior) or not a typedef variant of a user-facing type (if FLAGS contains STF_USER_VISIBLE). If T is not a type, then this just dispatches to strip_typedefs_expr. E.g. consider the following declarations: typedef const int ConstInt; typedef ConstInt* PtrConstInt; If T is PtrConstInt, this function returns a type representing const int*. In other words, if T is a typedef, the function returns the underlying type. The cv-qualification and attributes of the type returned match the input type. They will always be compatible types. The returned type is built so that all of its subtypes recursively have their typedefs stripped as well. This is different from just returning TYPE_CANONICAL (T) Because of several reasons: If T is a type that needs structural equality its TYPE_CANONICAL (T) will be NULL. TYPE_CANONICAL (T) desn't carry type attributes and loses template parameter names. If REMOVE_ATTRIBUTES is non-null, also strip attributes that don't affect type identity, and set the referent to true if any were stripped.

True if DECL is a constrained hidden friend as per [temp.friend]/9: A non-template friend declaration with a requires-clause shall be a definition. The ABI calls this a "member-like constrained friend" and mangles it like a member function to avoid collisions.

gcc/cp/decl.cc.signature: static void wrap_temporary_cleanups (tree init, tree guard)
gcc/cp/decl.cc.summary: We're initializing a local variable which has a cleanup GUARD. If there are any temporaries used in the initializer INIT of this variable, we need to wrap their cleanups with TRY_CATCH_EXPR (, GUARD) so that the variable will be cleaned up properly if one of them throws. Unfortunately, there's no way to express this properly in terms of nesting, as the regions for the temporaries overlap the region for the variable itself; if there are two temporaries, the variable needs to be the first thing destroyed if either of the temporary destructors throws. However, we only want to run the variable's cleanup if it actually got constructed. So we need to guard the temporary cleanups with the variable's cleanup if they are run on the normal path, but not if they are run on the exceptional path. We implement this by telling honor_protect_cleanup_actions to strip the variable cleanup from the exceptional path. Another approach could be to make the variable cleanup region enclose initialization, but depend on a flag to indicate that the variable is initialized; that's effectively what we do for arrays. But the current approach works fine for non-arrays, and has no code overhead in the usual case

gcc/cp/decl.cc.signature: tree start_enum (tree name, tree enumtype, tree underlying_type, tree attributes, bool scoped_enum_p, bool *is_new)
gcc/cp/decl.cc.summary: Begin compiling the definition of an enumeration type. NAME is its name, if ENUMTYPE is not NULL_TREE then the type has alredy been found. UNDERLYING_TYPE is the type that will be used as the storage for the enumeration type. This should be NULL_TREE if no storage type was specified. ATTRIBUTES are any attributes specified after the enum-key. SCOPED_ENUM_P is true if this is a scoped enumeration type. if IS_NEW is not NULL, gets TRUE iff a new type is created. Returns the type object, as yet incomplete. Also records info about it so that build_enumerator may be used to declare the individual values as they are read.
After processing and defining all the values of an enumeration type, install their decls in the enumeration type. ENUMTYPE is the type object.
Finishes the enum type. This is called only the first time an enumeration is seen, be it opaque or odinary. ENUMTYPE is the type object.

gcc/cp/decl.cc.signature: tree build_enumerator (tree name, tree value, tree enumtype, tree attributes, location_t loc)
gcc/cp/decl.cc.summary: Build and install a CONST_DECL for an enumeration constant of the enumeration type ENUMTYPE whose NAME and VALUE (if any) are provided. Apply ATTRIBUTES if available. LOC is the location of NAME. Assignment of sequential values by default is handled here.

Look for an enumerator with the given NAME within the enumeration type ENUMTYPE. This routine is used primarily for qualified name lookup into an enumerator in C++0x, e.g., enum class Color { Red, Green, Blue }; Color color = Color::Red; Returns the value corresponding to the enumerator, or NULL_TREE if no such enumerator was found.

True iff FN is an implicitly-defined default constructor.
Clobber the contents of *this to let the back end know that the object storage is dead when we enter the constructor or leave the destructor.

gcc/cp/decl.cc.signature: bool start_preparsed_function (tree decl1, tree attrs, int flags)
gcc/cp/decl.cc.summary: Create the FUNCTION_DECL for a function definition. DECLSPECS and DECLARATOR are the parts of the declaration; they describe the function's name and the type it returns, but twisted together in a fashion that parallels the syntax of C. FLAGS is a bitwise or of SF_PRE_PARSED (indicating that the DECLARATOR is really the DECL for the function we are about to process and that DECLSPECS should be ignored), SF_INCLASS_INLINE indicating that the function is an inline defined in-class. This function creates a binding context for the function body as well as setting up the FUNCTION_DECL in current_function_decl. For C++, we must first check whether that datum makes any sense. For example, "class A local_a(1,2);" means that variable local_a is an aggregate of type A, which should have a constructor applied to it with the argument list [1, 2]. On entry, DECL_INITIAL (decl1) should be NULL_TREE or error_mark_node, or may be a BLOCK if the function has been defined previously in this translation unit. On exit, DECL_INITIAL (decl1) will be error_mark_node if the function has never been defined, or a BLOCK if the function has been defined somewhere.

gcc/cp/decl.cc.signature: bool start_function (cp_decl_specifier_seq *declspecs, const cp_declarator *declarator, tree attrs)
gcc/cp/decl.cc.summary: Like start_preparsed_function, except that instead of a FUNCTION_DECL, this function takes DECLSPECS and DECLARATOR. Returns true on success. If the DECLARATOR is not suitable for a function, we return false, which tells the parser to skip the entire function.
Returns true iff an EH_SPEC_BLOCK should be created in the body of FN.

gcc/cp/decl.cc.signature: void do_push_parm_decls (tree decl, tree args, tree *nonparms)
gcc/cp/decl.cc.summary: Helper function to push ARGS into the current lexical scope. DECL is the function declaration. NONPARMS is used to handle enum constants.

Store the parameter declarations into the current function declaration. This is called after parsing the parameter declarations, before digesting the body of the function. Also install to binding contour return value identifier, if any.
Mark CDTOR's implicit THIS argument for returning, if required by the ABI.. Return the decl for THIS, if it is to be returned, and NULL otherwise.
Set the return value of the [cd]tor if the ABI wants that.
Do all the processing for the beginning of a destructor; set up the vtable pointers and cleanups for bases and members.

Do the necessary processing for the beginning of a function body, which in this case includes member-initializers, but not the catch clauses of a function-try-block. Currently, this means opening a binding level for the member-initializers (in a ctor), member cleanups (in a dtor), and capture proxies (in a lambda operator()).

Do the processing for the end of a function body. Currently, this means closing out the cleanups for fully-constructed bases and members, and in the case of the destructor, deleting the object if desired. Again, this is only meaningful for [cd]tors, since they are the only functions where there is a significant distinction between the main body and any function catch clauses. Handling, say, main() return semantics here would be wrong, as flowing off the end of a function catch clause for main() would also need to return 0.
Given a function, returns the BLOCK corresponding to the outermost level of curly braces, skipping the artificial block created for constructor initializers.
If FNDECL is a class's key method, add the class to the list of keyed classes that should be emitted.
Attempt to add a fix-it hint to RICHLOC suggesting the insertion of "return *this;" immediately before its location, using FNDECL's first statement (if any) to give the indentation, if appropriate.

Finish up a function declaration and compile that function all the way to assembler language output. The free the storage for the function definition. INLINE_P is TRUE if we just finished processing the body of an in-class inline function definition. (This processing will have taken place after the class definition is complete.)

gcc/cp/decl.cc.signature: tree grokmethod (cp_decl_specifier_seq *declspecs, const cp_declarator *declarator, tree attrlist)
gcc/cp/decl.cc.summary: Create the FUNCTION_DECL for a function definition. DECLSPECS and DECLARATOR are the parts of the declaration; they describe the return type and the name of the function, but twisted together in a fashion that parallels the syntax of C. This function creates a binding context for the function body as well as setting up the FUNCTION_DECL in current_function_decl. Returns a FUNCTION_DECL on success. If the DECLARATOR is not suitable for a function (it defines a datum instead), we return 0, which tells yyparse to report a parse error. May return void_type_node indicating that this method is actually a friend. See grokfield for more details. Came here with a `.pushlevel' . DO NOT MAKE ANY CHANGES TO THIS CODE WITHOUT MAKING CORRESPONDING CHANGES TO CODE IN `grokfield'.

VAR is a VAR_DECL. If its type is incomplete, remember VAR so that we can lay it out later, when and if its type becomes complete. Also handle constexpr variables where the initializer involves an unlowered PTRMEM_CST because the class isn't complete yet.
Called when a class type (given by TYPE) is defined. If there are any existing VAR_DECLs whose type has been completed by this declaration, update them now.

If DECL is of a type which needs a cleanup, build and return an expression to perform that cleanup here. Return NULL_TREE if no cleanup need be done. DECL can also be a _REF when called from split_nonconstant_init_1.
Return the FUNCTION_TYPE that corresponds to MEMFNTYPE, which can be a FUNCTION_DECL, METHOD_TYPE, FUNCTION_TYPE, pointer or reference to METHOD_TYPE or FUNCTION_TYPE, or pointer to member function.
DECL was originally constructed as a non-static member function, but turned out to be static. Update it accordingly.
Return which tree structure is used by T, or TS_CP_GENERIC if T is one of the language-independent trees.
Return the decl used to identify the COMDAT group into which DECL should be placed.
Returns the return type for FN as written by the user, which may include a placeholder for a deduced return type.

Complain if DECL has an undeduced return type.
Create a representation of the explicit-specifier with constant-expression of EXPR. COMPLAIN is as for tsubst.

gcc/tree.cc.summary: Callback called through walk_tree_1 to discover DECL_HAS_VALUE_EXPR_P VAR_DECLs which weren't marked yet, in that case marks them and walks their DECL_VALUE_EXPR expressions.
Callback called through traverse_noresize on the value_expr_for_decl hash table.

The value_expr_for_decl hash table can have mappings for trees which are only referenced from mappings of other trees in the same table, see PR118790. Without this routine, gt_cleare_cache could clear hash table slot of a tree which isn't marked but will be marked when processing later hash table slot of another tree which is marked. This function marks with the above helpers marks all the not yet marked DECL_HAS_VALUE_EXPR_P VAR_DECLs mentioned in DECL_VALUE_EXPR expressions of marked trees and in that case also recurses on their DECL_VALUE_EXPR.

gcc/tree.cc.signature: tree force_fit_type (tree type, const poly_wide_int_ref &cst, int overflowable, bool overflowed)
gcc/tree.cc.summary: We force the wide_int CST to the range of the type TYPE by sign or zero extending it. OVERFLOWABLE indicates if we are interested in overflow of the value, when >0 we are only interested in signed overflow, for <0 we are interested in any overflow. OVERFLOWED indicates whether overflow has already occurred. CONST_OVERFLOWED indicates whether constant overflow has already occurred. We force T's value to be within range of T's type (by setting to 0 or 1 all the bits outside the type's range). We set TREE_OVERFLOWED if, OVERFLOWED is nonzero, or OVERFLOWABLE is >0 and signed overflow occurs or OVERFLOWABLE is <0 and any overflow occurs We return a new tree node for the extended wide_int. The node is shared if no overflow flags are set.

Wrap a SAVE_EXPR around EXPR, if appropriate. Do this to any expression which may be used in more than one place, but must be evaluated only once. Normally, expand_expr would reevaluate the expression each time. Calling save_expr produces something that is evaluated and recorded the first time expand_expr is called on it. Subsequent calls to expand_expr just reuse the recorded value. The call to expand_expr that generates code that actually computes the value is the first call *at compile time*. Subsequent calls at compile time* generate code to use the saved value. This produces correct result provided that *at run time* control always flows through the insns made by the first expand_expr before reaching the other places where the save_expr was evaluated. You, the caller of save_expr, must make sure this is so. Constants, and certain read-only nodes, are returned with no SAVE_EXPR because that is safe. Expressions containing placeholders are not touched; see tree.def for an explanation of what these are used for.

Subroutine of stabilize_reference; this is called for subtrees of references. Any expression with side-effects must be put in a SAVE_EXPR to ensure that it is only evaluated once. We don't put SAVE_EXPR nodes around everything, because assigning very simple expressions to temporaries causes us to miss good opportunities for optimizations. Among other things, the opportunity to fold in the addition of a constant into an addressing mode often gets lost, e.g. "y[i+1] += x;". In general, we take the approach that we should not make an assignment unless we are forced into it - i.e., that any non-side effect operator should be allowed, and that cse should take care of coalescing multiple utterances of the same expression should that prove fruitful.

Stabilize a reference so that we can use it any number of times without causing its operands to be evaluated more than once. Returns the stabilized reference. This works by means of save_expr, so see the caveats in the comments about save_expr. Also allows conversion expressions whose operands are references. Any other kind of expression is returned unchanged.

Return OP, stripped of any conversions to wider types as much as is safe. Converting the value back to OP's type makes a value equivalent to OP. If FOR_TYPE is nonzero, we return a value which, if converted to type FOR_TYPE, would be equivalent to converting OP to type FOR_TYPE. OP must have integer, real or enumeral type. Pointers are not allowed! There are some cases where the obvious value we could return would regenerate to OP if converted to OP's type, but would not extend like OP to wider types. If FOR_TYPE indicates such extension is contemplated, we eschew such values. For example, if OP is (unsigned short)(signed char)-1, we avoid returning (signed char)-1 if FOR_TYPE is int, even though extending that to an unsigned short would regenerate OP, since the result of extending (signed char)-1 to (int) is different from (int) OP.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: static bool is_builtin_name (const char *name)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return true if NAME starts with __builtin_ or __sync_.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: bool called_as_built_in (tree node)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return true if NODE should be considered for inline expansion regardless of the optimization level. This means whenever a function is invoked with its "internal" name, which normally contains the prefix "__builtin".

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: bool get_object_alignment_2 (tree exp, unsigned int *alignp, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT *bitposp, bool addr_p)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Compute values M and N such that M divides (address of EXP - N) and such that N < M. If these numbers can be determined, store M in alignp and N in BITPOSP and return true. Otherwise return false and store BITS_PER_UNIT to alignp and any bit-offset to *bitposp. Note that the address (and thus the alignment) computed here is based on the address to which a symbol resolves, whereas DECL_ALIGN is based on the address at which an object is actually located. These two addresses are not always the same. For example, on ARM targets, the address &foo of a Thumb function foo() has the lowest bit set, whereas foo() itself starts on an even address. If ADDR_P is true we are taking the address of the memory reference EXP and thus cannot rely on the access taking place.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: bool get_object_alignment_1 (tree exp, unsigned int *alignp, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT *bitposp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: For a memory reference expression EXP compute values M and N such that M divides (&EXP - N) and such that N < M. If these numbers can be determined, store M in alignp and N in *BITPOSP and return true. Otherwise return false and store BITS_PER_UNIT to *alignp and any bit-offset to *bitposp.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: unsigned int get_object_alignment (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return the alignment in bits of EXP, an object.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: bool get_pointer_alignment_1 (tree exp, unsigned int *alignp, unsigned HOST_WIDE_INT *bitposp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: For a pointer valued expression EXP compute values M and N such that M divides (EXP - N) and such that N < M. If these numbers can be determined, store M in alignp and N in *BITPOSP and return true. Return false if the results are just a conservative approximation. If EXP is not a pointer, false is returned too.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: unsigned int get_pointer_alignment (tree exp)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return the alignment in bits of EXP, a pointer valued expression. The alignment returned is, by default, the alignment of the thing that EXP points to. If it is not a POINTER_TYPE, 0 is returned. Otherwise, look at the expression to see if we can do better, i.e., if the expression is actually pointing at an object whose alignment is tighter.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: unsigned string_length (const void *ptr, unsigned eltsize, unsigned maxelts)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Return the number of leading non-zero elements in the sequence [ PTR, PTR + MAXELTS ) where each element's size is ELTSIZE bytes. ELTSIZE must be a power of 2 less than 8. Used by c_strlen.

gcc/builtins.cc.signature: tree c_strlen (tree arg, int only_value, c_strlen_data *data, unsigned eltsize)
gcc/builtins.cc.summary: Compute the length of a null-terminated character string or wide character string handling character sizes of 1, 2, and 4 bytes. TREE_STRING_LENGTH is not the right way because it evaluates to the size of the character array in bytes (as opposed to characters) and because it can contain a zero byte in the middle. ONLY_VALUE should be nonzero if the result is not going to be emitted into the instruction stream and zero if it is going to be expanded. E.g. with i++ ? "foo" : "bar", if ONLY_VALUE is nonzero, constant 3 is returned, otherwise NULL, since len = c_strlen (ARG, 1); if (len) expand_expr (len, ...); would not evaluate the side-effects. If ONLY_VALUE is two then we do not emit warnings about out-of-bound accesses. Note that this implies the result is not going to be emitted into the instruction stream. Additional information about the string accessed may be recorded in DATA. For example, if ARG references an unterminated string, then the declaration will be stored in the DECL field. If the length of the unterminated string can be determined, it'll be stored in the LEN field. Note this length could well be different than what a C strlen call would return. ELTSIZE is 1 for norm

LEN must be a multiple of 1<<CTZ_LEN between MIN_LEN and MAX_LEN. The strategy is to issue one store_by_pieces for each power of two, from most to least significant, guarded by a test on whether there are at least that many bytes left to copy in LEN. ??? Should we skip some powers of two in favor of loops? Maybe start at the max of TO/LEN/word alignment, at least when optimizing for size, instead of ensuring O(log len) dynamic compares?

We store accesses in one of the two lists: PBEFORE_SP, and PNO_SP. If this expression or its only operand forces a sequence point, then everything up to the sequence point is stored in PBEFORE_SP. Everything else gets stored in PNO_SP. Once we return, we will have emitted warnings if any subexpression before such a sequence point could be undefined. On a higher level, however, the sequence point may not be relevant, and we'll merge the two lists. Example: (b++, a) + b; The call that processes the COMPOUND_EXPR will store the increment of B in PBEFORE_SP, and the use of A in PNO_SP. The higher-level call that processes the PLUS_EXPR will need to merge the two lists so that eventually, all accesses end up on the same list (and we'll warn about the unordered subexpressions b++ and b. A note on merging. If we modify the former example so that our expression becomes (b++, b) + a care must be taken not simply to add all three expressions into the final PNO_SP list. The function merge_tlist takes care of that by merging the before-SP list of the COMPOUND_EXPR into its after-SP list

Setup a TYPE_DECL node as a typedef representation. X is a TYPE_DECL for a typedef statement. Create a brand new ..._TYPE node (which will be just a variant of the existing ..._TYPE node with identical properties) and then install X as the TYPE_NAME of this brand new (duplicate) ..._TYPE node. The whole point here is to end up with a situation where each and every ..._TYPE node the compiler creates will be uniquely associated with AT MOST one node representing a typedef name. This way, even though the compiler substitutes corresponding ..._TYPE nodes for TYPE_DECL (i.e. "typedef name") nodes very early on, later parts of the compiler can always do the reverse translation and get back the corresponding typedef name. For example, given: typedef struct S MY_TYPE; MY_TYPE object; Later parts of the compiler might only know that `object' was of type `struct S' if it were not for code just below. With this code however, later parts of the compiler see something like: struct S' == struct S typedef struct S' MY_TYPE; struct S' object; And they can then deduce (from the node for type struct S') that the original object declaration was: MY_TYPE object; Being able to do this is important for

It only makes sense to do this for values of TYPE that are symbols. Some symbols should go before the next token, e.g. in: if flag) we want to insert the missing '(' immediately before "flag", giving: if (flag) rather than: if( flag) These use MTIK_INSERT_BEFORE_NEXT. Other symbols should go after the previous token, e.g. in: if (flag do_something (); we want to insert the missing ')' immediately after the "flag", giving: if (flag) do_something (); rather than: if (flag )do_something (); These use MTIK_INSERT_AFTER_PREV.
